text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The opposition centre-right Democratic Alliance Party boycotted a meeting of political parties, claiming it would be used for propaganda by the ruling Democrats.
- In a meeting with President Sali Berisha, Albania's political parties agreed to change the electoral law and procedures, as suggested by the Council of Europe last week.
- Albanians make up the greatest number of illegal immigrants in Italy, according to Italian daily Il Mondo.
- Government revenues in the first half of 1996 covered only 63 percent of expenditure.
- The European Union is to give 140 million ECUs to Albania between 1996-2000, as part of the EU PHARE programme, which provides technical aid to East European countries.
A political book "Nano and Berisha" by the journalist Ylli Polovina on Socialist Party head Fatos Nano and President Sali Berisha has topped the bestseller chart in Tirana.
- The current polio outbreak has claimed its fifth victim -- a 36-year-old man.
- The opposition Socialist Party has begun preparations for the upcoming local election.
- Five new judges and 10 assistants nominated by the High Council of Justice have started work in the Tirana district court.
- Trade unions in the eastern town of Librazhd are to hold a strike demanding compensation for bread price liberalisation.
- The European Commission has given $27 million to Albania for its balance of payments.
- The government will not return churches of historical value to the Orthodox Church, Teodor Laco, minister of culture, said.
